name: British Columbia
summary: The Union Flag with a crown at its centre across the upper part, above a golden setting sun over blue and white wavy bars. It is a banner of the province's arms, granted in 1906.
origin: The provincial arms were granted by King Edward VII in 1906. The flag, a banner of the shield, was adopted on 27 June 1960.

symbols.name: Union Flag with crown
symbols.description: The Union Flag in the upper third, with a gold crown in the centre.
symbols.meaning: British heritage and the province's name.

symbols.name: Setting sun
symbols.description: A gold sun setting over the sea.
symbols.meaning: British Columbia as Canada's westernmost province; the motto 'Splendor sine occasu' (Splendour without diminishment).

facts: Its setting sun reflects its position on the Pacific coast.
The motto on the arms is a pun on the British Empire, 'on which the sun never sets'.
It is the only provincial flag with the Union Flag covering its full width.
clues: A Union Flag with a crown above a golden setting sun over wavy blue and white lines.
Its sun sets over the westernmost province's ocean.
Its motto plays on a sun that never sets.
